claims.hypothesis: Can the strong field prevent fragmentation?

A strongly magnetized environment exerts an adequate support against rapid gravitational collapse, although the magnetic field could not hinder the fragmentation.

referee_caveats_inferred: Distance and hence all au scales, masses and densities are unspecified in the text
Reduced chi-squared of 9.39 indicates a poor formal fit; no priors or posterior sampling, only a grid with Lampton errors
DCF Q factor varies 0.28-0.5 and the 3.0-3.6 vs 4.0 mG spread is not propagated into B
Single temperature of 50 K for mass, sigma_th and model, taken from a region that avoids the cores
Binary-boundness uses 1-D velocities from another paper and a random-orientation factor
Line-of-sight inclination from the model is a model-dependent quantity used to turn B_pos into B

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Two ALMA Band 6 projects (2017.1.00101.S, 2018.1.00105.S) of raw data, probably tens of GB; the 12CO project 2013.1.00960.S adds more
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project codes and many imaging and DCF numbers are given, but the distance, spectral windows, imaging masks and the model grid set-up are not, and the polarization calibration is deferred to earlier papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The paper does not state that data are public and the magnetic-field model set-up (grid, density profile, ARTIST inputs) is too incomplete to redo from the text alone.
